These exercises follow the tasks on the slides of lecture 11, "Cluster analysis in practice". Write your code in the empty chunks, and answer the questions in a sentence or two under each chunk. Section 5 goes beyond the slides.

## Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(psych)
library(cluster)
library(simling)
```

## The data

`web_registers` holds the 480 web texts from six registers of lecture 9. The factor analysis from that lecture, without the redundant `pronouns`, gives each text a score on three dimensions:

```{r}
features <- select(web_registers, adverbs:word_length, -pronouns)
mda <- fa(features, nfactors = 3, rotate = "promax", fm = "minres")
scores <- bind_cols(select(web_registers, text, register), as_tibble(mda$scores))
scores
```

The research question: do the texts fall into groups by their linguistic features, and do those groups match the six registers? `?web_registers` gives the true model. Leave it closed until section 5.

## 4. How stable are the clusters?

### 4.1 Two halves

Split the texts at random into two halves, and fit k-means with three clusters to each half. Assign all 480 texts to the nearest centre of each solution with `nearest()`, and cross-tabulate the two assignments.

```{r}
set.seed(3)
half <- sample(rep(1:2, length.out = nrow(S)))
nearest <- function(X, centres) apply(X, 1, \(x) which.min(colSums((t(centres) - x)^2)))
```

```{r}

```

### 4.2 Three or six?

